newsitem.title: UK: Ford to cut 1,500 British jobs at Halewood -BBC.
newsitem.headline: Ford to cut 1,500 British jobs at Halewood -BBC.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. will cut 1,500 jobs at its giant Halewood plant in northwest England, one-third of the factory's work force, the British Broadcasting Corp. reported Wednesday.
Ford declined to comment on the report.

The automaker was scheduled to hold a meeting with unions led by the Transport and General Workers Union (TGWU) Thursday morning to discuss the future of the Halewood plant, which makes Ford's Escort model.

The company said it would not confirm any reports about possible job losses ahead of the meeting, which comes amid rumours of possible closure of the plant and speculation that the new Escort version, due in 1999, would not be built at Halewood.
Ford said Sunday that it would restructure but not close the plant.
Analysts said it was unlikely Ford would take the drastic measure of closing down a plant and cutting all 5,000 jobs.
But Halewood is seen by some analysts as one of the least productive Ford plants in Europe.
The current Escort, a subcompact built for the European market, is similar in design to the U.S. Escort and competes with General Motors Corp.'s Opel Astra and Volkswagen AG's Golf cars.
